title: Could old armour stop a bullet?
description: A qualified historical explanation of armour and firearms. Original narration; the museum objects are illustrative examples, not recordings of a ballistic test.

sections.title: Could armour stop a bullet?
sections.narration: Could old armour stop a bullet? Sometimes. The answer depends on the armour and the weapon.
bullet_points: Armour and the weapon both matter

sections.title: Rings and solid steel
sections.narration: Mail armour uses linked rings. Steel plate armour can deflect some blows away from the body.

sections.title: Adding another layer
sections.narration: When firearms spread, steel armour was hardened, thickened, or given a reinforcing layer over the breastplate.

sections.title: The proof was a dent
sections.narration: In proof tests, bullets hit some steel breastplates. A surviving dent showed that particular shot had stopped.

sections.title: Protection had limits
sections.narration: But one successful test was no universal guarantee. Armour and firearms evolved together for centuries; protection always had limits.
bullet_points: A specific test is not a universal guarantee
